title: Dex Agents CLI configuration
description: The configuration file of a Dex Agents CLI command, ~/.dex/agents/<harness>.yaml by default. It is YAML 1.2; this schema checks the parsed value. Every harness command in Python and TypeScript reads the same common fields and its own harness section. Do not put secrets in this file: provider keys come from the environment, and connector credentials stay in the connections that Dex Web authorizes. The schema cannot enforce this inside the open harness sections. Omit a field to take its default; null is never a valid value. The settings of one session may change model and system_prompt and may only narrow the rest; see session-settings.schema.json.
$comment: Patterns end with (?![\s\S]) rather than $, because Python's re lets $ match before a trailing newline and ECMAScript does not. The not schema repeats properties so that Ajv's strictRequired mode accepts it.

model.description: The model the agent calls, in the harness's own format, such as claude-opus-5-5 or a <provider>/<model> ID. Omitted: the harness command's default model. A harness command without a default model refuses to run until this is set.

system_prompt.description: The agent's instructions. Omitted, together with system_prompt_file: the harness's default instructions. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt_file.

system_prompt_file.description: A UTF-8 text file whose content is the agent's instructions, read when the command starts. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt.

dex.description: The Dex server the Worker and the Client connect to, and how they authenticate to it.

server.title: "auto" (dexcli dev on this machine), or the http or https URL of a Dex server, without user info
server.description: auto: reuse the running dexcli dev server of this machine, or start one. Otherwise the http or https URL of a Dex server, without user info. Its host is a DNS name whose last label starts with a letter, a dotted IPv4 address, or a bracketed IPv6 address. After the schema, the CLI core also checks that each IPv4 part is 0 or a decimal from 1 to 255 without a leading zero, that an IPv6 address is valid, that no DNS label starts with xn--, and that the port is at most 65535.

auth.description: How the Worker and the Client authenticate to the Dex server. Only this section turns authentication on: with mode none, or without this section, the command reads none of DEX_API_KEY, DEX_TOKEN_URL, DEX_SERVER_ID, DEX_CREDENTIAL, and DEX_CREDENTIAL_FILE. Any other mode needs dex.server set to a Dex server URL. The secret never goes in this file: the API key comes from DEX_API_KEY, and a bearer token from DEX_CREDENTIAL or a token file. A variable that is set and not empty after trimming overrides the matching field of the selected mode: DEX_TOKEN_URL overrides token_url, DEX_SERVER_ID overrides server_id, and DEX_CREDENTIAL_FILE overrides file.

mode.description: none: no credential. api_key: exchange the API key in DEX_API_KEY at token_url for short-lived access tokens scoped to server_id. bearer: send a bearer token, the value of DEX_CREDENTIAL (source env) or the content of a token file, read again for each call (source file).

token_url.description: api_key only. The token endpoint that exchanges the API key for access tokens: an https URL, or an http URL on localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, or [::1], without user info or a fragment. DEX_TOKEN_URL overrides it; one of the two is required. The host rules and the CLI core checks are those of dex.server.

server_id.description: api_key only. The Dex server ID that the access tokens are scoped to. DEX_SERVER_ID overrides it; one of the two is required.

source.description: bearer only, and required with it. env: the token is the value of DEX_CREDENTIAL. file: the token is the content of the file that file or DEX_CREDENTIAL_FILE names.

file.description: bearer with source file only. The file that holds the bearer token, such as one that another process rotates. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file. DEX_CREDENTIAL_FILE overrides it; one of the two is required.

api_key.description: Never: secrets come only from the environment.

credential.description: Never: secrets come only from the environment.

token.description: Never: secrets come only from the environment.

access_token.description: Never: secrets come only from the environment.

tls.description: How the Worker and the Client verify an https dex.server. An https dex.server turns TLS on, with the default trust store and the URL's host as the server name; these fields change that, and they need an https dex.server. DEX_TLS_CA_FILE and DEX_TLS_SERVER_NAME, when set and not empty after trimming, override them; the command reads them only for an https dex.server.

ca_file.description: A PEM file of root CAs to trust in addition to the default trust store, such as a private CA. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file. Omitted: the default trust store only.

server_name.description: The name the server certificate must match, sent as SNI, when it differs from the dex.server host: a DNS name or an IP address, without a port. Omitted: the dex.server host.

connectors.description: The connector tools the agent may call.

mcp.title: "auto" (the connectors MCP server of dexcli dev), or an http or https URL on 127.0.0.1, localhost, or [::1]
mcp.description: The connectors MCP server. auto: the server that dexcli dev provides. Otherwise its http or https URL on a loopback host: 127.0.0.1, localhost, or [::1], without user info. After the schema, the CLI core also checks that the port is at most 65535.

enabled.description: The connections whose operations the agent may call. Omitted: every authorized connection, with every operation its connector offers to agents. An empty list: no connector tools. An entry names a connector, which covers all of its connections, or connector/connection. A single-key map {"connector/connection": {"tools": [...]}} or {"connector": {"tools": [...]}} also limits the operations. Two entries must not cover the same connection.

mcp_servers.description: Remote MCP servers whose tools the agent may call over the Streamable HTTP transport, by server name: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, starting with a letter. The agent sees each tool as <server name>__<tool name>, and approval.always names it that way. Every call waits for approval unless trust_tool_annotations lets the server's hints mark the tool a read or an idempotent write. Keep secrets out of this file: a header value can take them from environment variables with ${NAME} references, which the Worker expands when the command starts. Session settings cannot change it: they ignore an mcp_servers key with a warning.

approval.description: Approval beyond what each tool already requires.

always.description: Tool names, as the agent sees them, whose every call waits for approval, in addition to the tools whose connector or local tool policy asks for it.

workspace.description: The only directory the local file tools may read and write, and the working directory of shell commands. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file. dex-agents-pi defaults to the directory the command starts in instead, and uses it only as the working directory of its own tools.

local_tools.description: Tools that act on this machine. Reads run without approval; writes, browser clicks, form fills, and submits wait for approval; each shell command waits for approval unless it matches the allow list.

files.description: Read, write, list, and search files inside workspace.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may run shell commands at all.

allow.description: Commands that run without approval. A command matches only when its whole text equals an entry exactly; every other command waits for approval.

browser.description: Drive a local browser. The browser is downloaded the first time the agent uses it.

media.description: Where the images of a session are stored: the images attached with /image and the images that connector tools return. Session state keeps only a reference to each image; the bytes stay in this store, one copy per distinct image, named by its SHA-256. Every Worker of a session must reach the same store. Sessions cannot change it: session settings ignore a media key with a warning. Credentials never go in this file: an s3 store reads them from the environment or the standard AWS chain.

store.title: "auto" (a directory on this machine), or s3://<bucket> or s3://<bucket>/<prefix>
store.description: auto: a directory on this machine, ~/.dex/agents/media, which keeps its own copy of each image, never a link to the original file. Otherwise s3://<bucket> or s3://<bucket>/<prefix> for an S3 bucket, which Workers on other machines can reach too. The bucket name has 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, or hyphens and starts and ends with a letter or digit; the prefix is printable ASCII without spaces. An s3 store needs the S3 support of the agents library: the dex-agents[s3] extra in Python, the @aws-sdk/client-s3 package in TypeScript.

endpoint.description: The http or https URL of an S3-compatible service, such as http://127.0.0.1:9000; omitted, AWS S3. Only valid with an s3 store. With an endpoint, the bucket is addressed in the URL path, as most S3-compatible services need. The host rules and the CLI core checks are those of dex.server.

sessions.description: How the command keeps its sessions. Session settings cannot change it: they ignore a sessions key with a warning.

summary.description: Whether each session keeps an indexed summary, its title, last activity time, and turn count, which the sessions subcommand shows. auto: on when dex.server is auto, the dexcli dev of this machine that the command reuses or starts, and off for a Dex server URL. on: always. off: never. With the summary, the title, the first 80 Unicode code points of the session's first message, is in the server's search index, readable by anyone who can search its Flows, and the Worker registers the index keys text1, datetime1, and int1, which can fail its start on a server with PostgreSQL search whose namespace already uses these keys with other types or has no free key of these types. Turning it off later stops new writes; values written before stay.

lease_ttl_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, a session's terminal lease lasts without a renewal; from 10 to 3600. The command renews it every third of that and releases it when it exits, so a waiting command takes the session over at once. A command that was killed or paused holds the session until its lease expires. The environment variable DEX_AGENTS_SESSION_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS overrides it.

claude.description: Options of the Claude Agent SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

openai.description: Options of the OpenAI Agents SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

pydantic_ai.description: Options of the Pydantic AI command. Omitted: its defaults.

deepagents.description: Options of the Deep Agents command. Omitted: its defaults.

google_adk.description: Options of the Google ADK command. Omitted: its defaults.

vercel_ai.description: Options of the Vercel AI SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

mastra.description: Options of the Mastra command. Omitted: its defaults.

pi.description: Options of the Pi command. Omitted: its defaults.

builtin.description: Options of the built-in agent loop command. Omitted: its defaults.

model.description: A model ID in the harness's own format, such as claude-opus-5-5 or openai/gpt-5-mini. Any non-empty string; the harness checks it.

tool_name.description: A tool name: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, or dots.

operation_name.description: A connector operation: its snake-case name, such as get_message, or its operationId, such as getMessage. Both spellings name the same operation: an operationId is compared after the connectors library's lowerCamelToSnake conversion, which keeps acronym runs together, so listStoryIDs is list_story_ids and getHTTPResponse is get_http_response.

connector_key.description: A connector ID, or connector/connection. A connection name has at most 256 characters, no slash, no control character, and no leading or trailing space, as Dex Web requires.

connector_entry.title: a connector ID or connector/connection, such as slack or slack/team, or a map with one such key and a tools list

tools.description: The connector operations the agent may call, by snake-case name or operationId. Two entries must not name the same operation.

url.description: The server's Streamable HTTP endpoint: an https URL, or an http URL on localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, or [::1], without user info or a fragment. The host rules and the CLI core checks are those of dex.server. The URL is used as written, never expanded, so it must not hold a secret.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent with every request to the server, such as Authorization, by header name: 1 to 256 HTTP token characters. A value is printable ASCII. Each ${NAME} in it is replaced by the value of the environment variable NAME when the command starts; NAME has ASCII letters, digits, and underscores and does not start with a digit. A variable that is not set, is empty, or holds anything but printable ASCII stops the command. Any other $ stays as written. A value may be literal; put each secret in a ${NAME} reference instead. The command never prints, logs, or stores the expanded values.

^[!#$%&'*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]{1,256}(?![\\.description: A header value: printable ASCII, where ${ always starts a ${NAME} reference.

trust_tool_annotations.description: Whether the server's readOnlyHint and idempotentHint annotations, and the effects it declares by the Dex MCP conventions, pick each tool's effect. false: every call of the server's tools waits for approval and runs at most once. true: a tool the server marks read-only or idempotent runs without approval, unless approval.always names it, and may be retried. Set it only for a server whose hints you trust.

harness_options.description: Harness options. Each harness command defines its own fields and ignores the sections of other harnesses.
